plan.title: bug(lifecycle): origin GitHub updates after ingest are not fail-closed at activate; reconcile:issues lacks the documented stale-content bucket

narratives.Description: After issue:ingest, promote/activate/preflight do not re-read GitHub. A later origin update, especially a comment that supersedes the body, is invisible and workers implement the snapshot. reconcile:issues lacks the stale-content bucket the refinement and sync skills document.
narratives.Overview:
**TL;DR: after `issue:ingest`, a GitHub body or comment change is not mechanically visible to promote / activate / preflight. Workers implement the snapshotted xBRIEF. `reconcile:issues` does not implement the stale-content bucket the refinement and sync skills document. #2143 is prose-only. First ship is one fail-closed tripwire at implementation intent, not auto-merge of origin into the brief.**

## What is true today

- **Ingest is live-first.** `fetchIssue` prefers GitHub, then cache (#1714). Comments are fetched live and folded into the proposed brief (#2143 ingest path).
- **Promote / activate / preflight do not re-read the origin.** They move folders and flip status.
- **`task reconcile:issues`** reports open vs closed vs unlinked (and completed-status drift). It does **not** compare origin `updated_at` to the brief `updated` timestamp.
- **Skill text disagrees.** `deft-directive-refinement` Phase 3 and `deft-directive-sync` Phase 5 say reconcile / sync will flag **stale** when the issue is newer than the brief, then walk the operator. That bucket is not on the engine.
- **#309 D12** already decided: detect mid-lifecycle origin change; never auto-update the brief; preserve intentional divergence. Detection at activate / dispatch is missing.

The cache-fresh inventory gate is a different problem (queue inventory, 24h + open-set drift). It does not keep an already-ingested brief current with its origin.

## Why this bites

GitHub remains the origin. After ingest the xBRIEF is the working source of truth and is often *ahead* of the issue (file scope, chosen option, extra AC). Auto-applying origin onto the brief would clobber that. The hole is the opposite: a **later** origin change (especially a comment that supersedes the body) is invisible unless an agent happens to re-fetch comments.

**Dogfood (#3351):** the investigation brief was ingested from the original body. A designer then posted the branch-3 disposition and successor (#3360) **in comments** and closed the issue. A worker still running the ingested brief would have treated the body as current. Hold + handoff avoided that. The lifecycle verbs would not have stopped it.

Same class as #2126 / #2143 (body-only dispatch shipped the wrong fix), now after a valid ingest snapshot instead of at first read.

## Thin first ship (#3265)

One fail-closed check, one remediation. Do **not** auto-write the brief.

At `scope:activate` or `xbrief:preflight` (implementation-intent, not every promote):

- If the brief has an `x-xbrief/github-issue` (or accepted alias) origin, fetch the live issue.
- If origin `updated_at` is newer than the brief `updated` / `xBRIEFInfo.updated`, exit 1.
- Remediation: re-read body + comments (#2143), then either refresh the brief or record intentional divergence (and bump brief `updated` so the gate stays quiet).

`updated_at` is noisy (labels, “lgtm”). Acceptable for v1 if the action is look-then-dispose. A body+comments hash stored at ingest is a later tightening, not this ship.

Also close the skill/engine lie: either teach `reconcile:issues` the documented stale-content bucket, or change the skills to match what the verb actually reports.

## Out of scope

- Auto-merging GitHub into the xBRIEF
- Using `cache:fetch-all` as the fix
- Fail-closed on every `scope:promote`
- Changing #309 D12 (detect, do not silent-overwrite)

## Acceptance sketch

- Activate / preflight of an origin-linked brief fails closed when the live issue `updated_at` is newer than the brief, with a remediation that names re-read + dispose (not overwrite).
- A fixture: ingest, then a newer origin timestamp, then activate/preflight exits 1; after recording divergence or refreshing the brief, the gate passes.
- Refinement / sync prose and `reconcile:issues` agree on whether a stale-content bucket exists.
- No test or skill change that auto-applies origin text onto the brief.

## Relates

#309 D12 (origin freshness, no auto-update), #1714 (ingest live-first), #2143 (body then comments), #1938 (TOCTOU on mutable externals), #3265 (thin fail-closed), #3351 (comment-supersedes-body after ingest).
narratives.UserStory: As an implementer, I want activate/preflight to fail closed when the live GitHub origin is newer than the brief, so that I re-read comments before coding against a stale snapshot.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Put the tripwire in packages/core/src/preflight (xbrief:preflight / implementation-intent), not every promote and not scope:activate (3360 owns activate). If the brief has an x-xbrief/github-issue origin and live updated_at is newer than xBRIEFInfo.updated, exit 1 with remediation: re-read body+comments then refresh or record intentional divergence (bump brief updated). Do not auto-write origin onto the brief. Teach task reconcile:issues a stale-content bucket or change refinement/sync Phase 5 prose to match the verb. Fixture: ingest, newer origin timestamp, preflight exits 1; after dispose the gate passes. CHANGELOG #3363.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an origin-linked brief whose live GitHub issue updated_at is newer than xBRIEFInfo.updated, when xbrief:preflight (or the chosen implementation-intent gate) runs, it exits 1 and the remediation names re-read body+comments then dispose, not overwrite.

Given a fixture that ingests then advances the origin timestamp, when preflight runs it exits 1. After recording divergence or refreshing the brief, the same gate exits 0. No test auto-applies origin text onto the brief.
Given refinement/sync prose and task reconcile:issues, when this lands they agree on whether a stale-content bucket exists. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] cites #3363.
